description: REMOTE-HEAVY profile - NOT the committed default. Selected by pointing DARCI_HOST_PROFILE at this file; host-profile.json stays all-local and keyless so a fresh clone boots with no credentials. This profile moves the TWO classes anything actually requests at runtime - chat.balanced (every toolkit, research, innovation and knowledge call) and code.generate - onto the remote OpenAI-compatible proxy, and keeps embeddings and the fast coding path local. No secret lives here: api_key_env names the environment variable and HostProfile.Validate() refuses to start if it is unset.
WARNING_READ_BEFORE_USE: coder-120b is a REASONING model and this profile is NOT SAFE until the caller token budgets are raised. Measured against this endpoint on 2026-11-12 with a realistic reasoning-heavy prompt: max_tokens 1024 -> empty, 4096 -> empty, 8192 -> empty, 16384 -> complete (7528 completion tokens). The model spends the whole budget thinking and emits no content, which OpenAiCompatibleModelProvider correctly reports as REMOTE_EMPTY_COMPLETION. A host profile CANNOT fix this: ModelProviderConfig has no max_tokens field, and the callers pass their own - OllamaClient.Generate hardcodes 1024 (Darci.Tools/Ollama/OllamaClient.cs:36) and ModelRouter hardcodes 4096 (Darci.Coding/ModelRouter.cs:23). Both are below the measured floor. Raise those, or add a per-provider max_tokens to ModelProviderConfig, before binding chat.balanced here.

litellm.note: Same proxy as host-profile.hybrid.json, verified 2026-11-12: GET /v1/models lists coder-120b among 7 models. The base URL INCLUDES /v1 - the proxy answers on both / and /v1, but /v1 is the canonical OpenAI root that /chat/completions is appended to. A hard prompt takes 35-38s, so timeout_minutes 10 is ample; the latency, not the ceiling, is the thing to watch.

chat.fast.note: Local. ASPIRATIONAL tier - no genuinely small model is installed, so this is the same 9B as chat.balanced. Nothing in the codebase requests chat.fast today.

chat.balanced.note: REMOTE, and this is the lever: every call through OllamaClient.Generate - toolkit, research agents, innovation synthesis, knowledge assessment, critics - asks for this class. It is the highest-volume text class by a wide margin, which is exactly why it is the one worth moving and the one most exposed to the token-budget problem in WARNING_READ_BEFORE_USE. OllamaClient sends max_tokens 1024, which measured EMPTY on this model.

chat.deep.note: REMOTE. Bound for completeness; nothing in the codebase requests chat.deep today, so this binding has no runtime effect until something does.

classify.intent.note: Stays local on purpose: classification is high-volume and latency-sensitive, and a 35s remote round trip per classification would dominate any loop. Nothing requests this class today either.

embed.text.note: STAYS LOCAL, and this one is not a preference. The proxy also fronts nomic-embed-text, but the stored vectors must stay comparable: switching the embedding model - or even the same model behind a different server - risks invalidating every embedding already in the knowledge graph and the coding workspaces. Re-embedding everything is the price of changing this.

code.generate.note: REMOTE. The 120B coder in place of the local 7B - this is the tier with the most to gain. ModelRouter sends max_tokens 4096, which also measured EMPTY on a reasoning-heavy prompt; see WARNING_READ_BEFORE_USE.

code.fast.note: Stays local on purpose - this is the fast/cheap iteration path, and keeping it local preserves a working coder when the remote is unavailable or slow. Also the fallback worth having while the remote budgets are unresolved.
